verdict: 2026-08-03 22:26 PDT — Not sound yet. The centralized runner, declarative pass/context tables, standard-library concurrency, routing data, and `jsonschema` validation are appropriate. However, the publication model cannot provide its promised round-level atomicity, and the model override separates model identity from the metadata required by the size guard.

findings.title: Two renames do not form an atomic review round
findings.claim: The architecture represents one logical review round as two independently replaced stable files. Staging both files first prevents staging failures from publishing partial output, but the subsequent `os.replace` loop can still publish the first artifact and fail on the second. The runner explicitly acknowledges this is not a multi-file transaction, despite AC-5 and the skill presenting both-or-neither promotion as an invariant. This publication pattern will also be copied by every future critic added to the altitude.
findings.alternative: Write every result into one immutable, round-specific directory, fsync it, then publish the completed round with one atomic directory rename or atomic current-round pointer. Make consumers resolve artifacts only through that committed round reference.
findings.win: Replaces a probabilistic sequence of renames with one atomic commit point, eliminating mixed/partial review rounds and centralizing the invariant for all future critics.

findings.title: The model override bypasses the routing contract's metadata
findings.claim: `--model` changes the live model id while the size guard continues using the configured route's `contextLength`. Model identity and the metadata needed to run it safely are therefore sourced from different records. A smaller override can pass local preflight using the routed model's larger window and fail only after making the API request; a larger override is constrained by unrelated metadata. This makes the new public override contract structurally incompatible with the fail-closed routing design.
findings.alternative: Make overrides select or supply a complete route record—model id plus context length—or remove the raw override and require temporary routing-table entries. If ad hoc model ids are essential, resolve and verify their live context metadata before assembly.
findings.win: Restores one authoritative model contract, makes the preflight guard apply to the model actually called, and removes an inconsistent execution path from the runner.
